newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine rains destroyed 200,000 hectares wheat.
newsitem.headline: Argentine rains destroyed 200,000 hectares wheat.

text.p: Storms last week destroyed 200,000 hectares of Argentina's wheat crop and produced varying degrees of quality damage to between 700,000 tonnes and 1.0 million tonnes, a government official said Tuesday.

"There are about 200,000 hectares lost," Food Under Secretary Felix Cirio told Reuters by telephone. "In addition we estimate that in the same area there are between 700,000 tonnes and 1.0 million tonnes with varying sorts of quality problems."

But Cirio said the government would not necessarily cut its 1996/97 production estimate of 14.9 million tonnes. He said that a new estimate to be released later this week would incorporate analysis of satellite photographs for the first time and would also have to take into account better than expected yields from early harvesting.
"I can't say which way the estimate is going to change, up or down," he said.
Cirio said that part of the wheat with quality problems will still be good enough to mix with good quality wheat from other areas. But some of it is totally lost.
"It is still very difficult to say how much exactly has been lost," he said.
Argentine regulations allow wheat mixes to include up to three percent of grains with quality problems.

The government has been working since Friday on assessing the damage from torrential rain and wind in the heart of the country's southern wheat belt last week, but will not have a final assessment of the damage until later in the week.
Argentine wheat prices have jumped on nervousness about the rain, amid rumors that as much as two million tonnes of the crop had been damaged.
